scope: Four reusable prerequisite corrections; topic claims, teaching guides, existing associations and all age intervals are unchanged.

before.reason: Paraphrasing requires the ability to identify main ideas and summarise; learners must extract key ideas before restating them in own words

after.reason: Identifying and recording main ideas in multi-paragraph written texts supports paraphrasing, but accurate restatement of heard or viewed material can be demonstrated orally without independent print reading or written notes. Retain the complete oral key-idea/detail and own-words requirements; written note-taking remains useful support.

changes.discriminatingCounterexample: A child hears an unfamiliar passage and accurately restates its central meaning and supporting details in fresh spoken words; independently reading several paragraphs and recording written notes has not been demonstrated. The complete oral claim succeeds while the complete written-notes prerequisite remains unassessed.

before.reason: Informative writing requires knowing 'genre', 'audience', 'purpose', and 'detail' as concepts

after.reason: Writing-process vocabulary helps explain composing choices, but naming a topic and conveying relevant facts through drawing, dictation or writing does not require mastery of the entire compose/plan/draft/revise/edit/proofread/genre glossary. Retain all informative content requirements; the vocabulary remains useful support.

changes.discriminatingCounterexample: A child dictates a named topic plus three accurate facts and labels an informative drawing, but cannot correctly explain draft/revise/proofread/genre or distinguish all writing-process terms. This satisfies the entire drawing/dictation/writing informative claim without mastery of the broad glossary.

before.reason: Writing simple narratives requires 'narrative', 'sequence', 'beginning', 'middle', 'ending' as shared vocabulary

after.reason: Writing-process vocabulary supports reflection on narratives, but a child can independently write sequenced sentences with time words and a beginning, middle and ending/reaction without correctly naming every writing-process or genre term. Retain all simple-narrative requirements; the glossary remains useful support.

changes.discriminatingCounterexample: A child independently writes a three-sentence event sequence with temporal words and a clear reaction/ending but cannot explain genre/audience/proofread. The full simple-narrative criteria succeed; the distinct glossary does not.

before.reason: Oral composition requires vocabulary like 'compose', 'sentence', and 'sequence' to participate meaningfully in the exercise

after.reason: Writing-process vocabulary supports discussion of oral rehearsal, but saying and repeating an intended complete sentence and practising it with a partner before writing does not require mastery of the broad writing-process glossary. Retain the full rehearsal procedure; the vocabulary remains useful support.

changes.discriminatingCounterexample: A child says and repeats a complete intended sentence, retains it and rehearses with a partner before writing, but cannot define compose/revise/genre. All rehearsal evidence succeeds while the broad process glossary is not mastered.

sourceRoleReview: NCERT role-specific assessment/material and remaining complete-claim compatibility review is separate. Conditional candidate associations remain withheld and all source dispositions are unchanged.
notInferred: No new topic, difficulty level or language-specific duplicate.
No automatic R1/R2 or English-to-other-language mastery transfer.
No change to expressive-reading print-direction and sight-word hard paths.
No learner estimate reset, score transfer or downstream publication.
